text: A Brisco County audit released Tuesday found $4.8 million in road maintenance funds missing from the fiscal 2025 works budget, with auditors saying the money was moved through three internal accounts and never reached scheduled resurfacing projects. The report traced the gap to transfers approved by former infrastructure director Hale Wen, who resigned in March. County finance staff said invoices and contractor records did not match the ledger, leaving 17 rural miles ungraded and two bridge repairs delayed. Commissioners have ordered a forensic review and frozen discretionary spending in the roads division. For the sector, the finding raises fresh scrutiny on municipal capital controls and could tighten oversight of local infrastructure budgets statewide.
